I’m validating the correct GCP runtime shape now, including Pub/Sub delivery and the AI hosting choice, before turning this into issues.

Live GitHub inventory found 10 open issues, no GitHub environments, no Actions secrets or variables, and only the CI workflow. I could not inspect an actual GCP project, so this assesses repository readiness, not deployed state.

## Priority findings

### P0 — No durable shared runtime

Evidence:

- Every process creates an isolated in-memory backend: `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:18-20`, `cmd/foundpet-service/main.go:19-22`, `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:16-18`, `cmd/notification-service/main.go:13-15`, `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:31-34`.
- UI and service collection names disagree: `lost_pets` at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:297-300` versus `lostPets` at `cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:65-72`; likewise `found_pets` at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:440-443` versus `foundPets` at `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:68-75`.
- The matcher reads one hard-coded candidate, `lost-101`, at `cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:78-105`.
- The match API seeds fake production-looking matches when state is empty at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:480-556`.
- Only memory implementations exist in `pkg/store/store.go:25-109`, `pkg/pubsub/pubsub.go:22-62`, and `pkg/blob/blob.go:31-100`.

Suggested issue: `feat(runtime): implement one durable shared report-to-match path`

Acceptance criteria:

- Implement Firestore state and GCS blob adapters using ADC.
- Define canonical collections and production data models.
- Production startup must reject memory adapters.
- Remove automatic demo seeding and hard-coded candidate IDs from production mode.
- Run Firestore/Pub/Sub/storage emulators or equivalent shared local dependencies in Compose.
- Prove a report survives service restart and is visible to another process.
- Add an emulator-backed and deployed smoke test for one vertical cascade.

Dependencies/duplicates: closed #3, #23, #90, and #93 are stale or only implemented interfaces/UI wiring; #66 is infrastructure-only.

### P0 — Pub/Sub and the Cloud Run worker model do not work

Evidence:

- Each binary owns a separate `MemoryPubSub`, so publishers cannot reach subscribers across containers.
- OpenTofu creates topics only, with no subscriptions: `infra/opentofu/modules/pubsub/main.tf:1-11`.
- `pet-matcher` and `notification-service` never listen on `$PORT`: `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:15-31`, `cmd/notification-service/main.go:13-26`.
- Both are nevertheless declared as Knative Cloud Run Services: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:1-18`, `deploy/cloudrun/notification-service.yaml:1-18`.

A Cloud Run Service ingress container must listen on its injected port. Google also recommends Pub/Sub push for Cloud Run services; pull-based workloads should deliberately use a worker pool instead. [Cloud Run container contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract), [Cloud Run autoscaling](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling), [subscription types](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-overview).

Suggested issue: `feat(pubsub): add authenticated Cloud Run push consumers`

Acceptance criteria:

- Add real Pub/Sub publishers and one subscription per consumer.
- Prefer authenticated push endpoints for matcher and notification handlers; otherwise document and provision worker pools.
- Grant the Pub/Sub push identity only `run.invoker` on its target.
- Return 2xx only after successful processing; temporary failures must produce redelivery.
- Provision ack/retry/retention/DLQ settings and DLQ subscriptions in OpenTofu.
- Verify authenticated delivery, redelivery, poison-message handling, and emulator/local behavior.

Dependencies/duplicates: #91 overlaps retry/DLQ but does not solve the missing transport or invalid Cloud Run execution model; its implementation proposal should be rewritten around subscription policy. Closed #22 promised subscriptions but created only topics.

### P0 — “Completed” GCS upload support is still a mock

Evidence:

- The upload handler constructs `MemoryBlobStore` per request: `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:772-795`.
- The generated URL contains literal `sig=mock-sig`: `pkg/blob/blob.go:75-99`.
- `foundpet-service` reserves but never uses the blob dependency: `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:14-27`.
- The storage bucket has no CORS or explicit public-access-prevention policy: `infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`.

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #62 rather than file a duplicate.

Additional acceptance criteria:

- Generate GCS V4 signed uploads with bounded object prefix, content type, size, and expiry.
- Verify object metadata before creating a found-pet record.
- Enforce bucket public-access prevention; signed URLs remain compatible with it.
- Restrict CORS to configured frontend origins and required methods/headers.
- Add orphan-upload cleanup and emulator/integration coverage.

Relevant guidance: [public access prevention and signed URLs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/public-access-prevention), [Cloud Storage CORS](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cross-origin).

### P0 — Authentication closure is stale; production exposure would expose mutations

Evidence:

- Routes are registered without authentication middleware at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71`.
- Anyone can confirm/reject matches at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:576-618`, send a purported “secure” contact message at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652`, or mark a pet reunited at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:661-699`.
- Lost-pet submissions accept reporter contact data at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267-300`.
- There is no user/session implementation in `go.mod:1-3` or the service startup path.

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #63.

Acceptance criteria:

- Integrate an OIDC provider or Identity Platform and validate sessions server-side.
- Enforce ownership/authorization on every state-changing or contact-data endpoint.
- Return redacted public DTOs.
- Add CSRF protection where cookie sessions are used.
- Audit authorization decisions and add negative integration tests.
- Make #94’s lifecycle endpoints depend on this work.

### P0 — Production AI inference is completely unprovisioned

Evidence:

- The client defaults to `http://localhost:11434`: `pkg/ollama/client.go:16`, `pkg/ollama/client.go:45-56`.
- The matcher manifest supplies no `OLLAMA_HOST`, model service, authentication, or GPU, and allocates only 2 CPU/2 GiB: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:9-18`.
- OpenTofu has no model-serving resource: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:16-39`.

Suggested issue: `feat(ai): provision private Gemma 4 inference for production`

Acceptance criteria:

- Record an architecture decision: private Cloud Run GPU Ollama versus managed Vertex AI.
- If retaining Ollama, provision an authenticated internal GPU Cloud Run service, set `OLLAMA_HOST`, model loading/startup probes, request timeout, concurrency, maximum instances, and quota.
- Do not expose Ollama publicly.
- Benchmark representative images for quality, p50/p95 latency, cold start, throughput, and cost.
- Add circuit breaking, bounded retries, and a user-visible deferred/retry state.
- Add model/version provenance to results.

Google now documents Gemma 4/Ollama on GPU Cloud Run, but it requires materially different resources and explicit cost/concurrency controls. [Gemma 4 with Ollama](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/tutorials/gpu-gemma-with-ollama), [Cloud Run GPU requirements](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu).

### P0 — No production build, release, or deploy pipeline

Evidence:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-187` contains validation only.
- All images use mutable `gcr.io/petspotr/*:latest`: `infra/opentofu/variables.tf:12-40` and every `deploy/cloudrun/*.yaml`.
- The deployment guide assumes an already-existing image and manually replaces a service: `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:82-105`.
- `Dockerfile:8` sends the entire repository into the build context, and there is no `.dockerignore`.
- GitHub currently has zero environments, Actions secrets, and variables.

Container Registry writes stopped in 2025; Artifact Registry is the supported target. [Artifact Registry transition](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/transition/transition-from-gcr).

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #13, preferably retitled `chore(cd): build and deploy immutable Cloud Run revisions`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Provision regional Artifact Registry repositories.
- Authenticate GitHub using Workload Identity Federation, never a service-account key.
- Build each image once per commit and deploy by digest.
- Generate SBOM/vulnerability results and fail on the agreed severity policy.
- Add protected staging/production GitHub environments and promotion rules.
- Choose one deployment authority—OpenTofu or manifests—and remove drift between them.
- Run post-deploy smoke checks, support traffic rollback, and record deployed SHA/digest.
- Add `.dockerignore` covering `.git`, local credentials, state, reports, and generated WIF credential files.

### P1 — Least-privilege identity and ingress are absent

Evidence:

- Cloud Run resources specify only name, location, and image: `infra/opentofu/modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-54`.
- No user-managed service accounts, IAM bindings, invoker policies, or ingress settings exist.
- Outputs call every service URL “Public”: `infra/opentofu/outputs.tf:1-24`.

Suggested action: expand/retitle open #66 to `feat(infra): enforce service identities and Cloud Run ingress`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Dedicated service account per service.
- Resource-scoped Firestore, Storage, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, and invoker roles.
- Only the intended browser entrypoint is unauthenticated.
- Matcher/notification endpoints accept only authenticated Pub/Sub delivery.
- Decide whether public traffic uses direct `run.app` or an external load balancer; if the latter, disable direct public ingress and add Armor/rate-limiting policy.
- Avoid the Compute Engine default service account.
- Add IAM policy tests and document the trust graph.

Google recommends user-managed identities with minimal roles and layered ingress plus IAM. [Cloud Run service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/service-identity), [Cloud Run ingress](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/ingress).

### P1 — Infrastructure cannot safely bootstrap or support environments

Evidence:

- No backend block or environment structure exists: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:1-39`.
- Required Google APIs are not enabled in code.
- The provider constraint is broad, `~> 5.0`: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:1-8`.
- `.terraform.lock.hcl` is ignored at `.gitignore:16-22`; the local ignored lock currently resolves old provider 5.45.2.
- Documentation directs developers to apply directly from a laptop: `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:82-89`.
- Infra tests check only file/resource-string existence: `infra/infra_test.go:10-39`.

Suggested issue: `chore(infra): add remote state and environment bootstrapping`

Acceptance criteria:

- Bootstrap a private, versioned, access-controlled GCS state bucket.
- Commit the dependency lock file and pin intentionally reviewed provider ranges.
- Separate dev/staging/prod projects or roots with explicit variables and labels.
- Enable required APIs declaratively.
- Add CI plan output, policy checks, approval-gated apply, and drift detection.
- Document ADC-based local planning; prohibit downloaded service-account keys.
- Add semantic IaC tests, not only string-existence checks.

Google recommends a Cloud Storage backend and automated plan/apply workflow. [Terraform security practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/best-practices/security), [Terraform operations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/best-practices/operations).

### P1 — Data protection, indexes, and disaster recovery are undefined

Evidence:

- Firestore is a bare regional database: `infra/opentofu/modules/firestore/main.tf:1-5`.
- No PITR, scheduled backup, deletion protection, TTL, or indexes exist.
- The bucket sets `force_destroy = true`: `infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`.
- Versioning is enabled without lifecycle limits, creating unbounded noncurrent-version cost.
- The region defaults to `us-central1` with no availability/RPO decision: `infra/opentofu/variables.tf:6-10`.

Suggested issue: `feat(data): define RPO, backups, indexes, and restore drills`

Acceptance criteria:

- Decide regional versus multi-region Firestore before first production creation.
- Set production deletion protection, PITR, and scheduled backups.
- Declare every required composite/geospatial/query index in code.
- Set `force_destroy=false` in production.
- Choose soft-delete/versioning/lifecycle policy and cap retained noncurrent versions.
- Define RPO/RTO and execute a documented Firestore and GCS restore drill.
- Monitor backup failures and storage growth.

Dependencies/duplicates: closed #93 covers API filtering, not Firestore indexing. No open issue covers recovery. [Firestore DR](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/disaster-recovery), [Firestore indexes as Terraform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/standard-indexing), [GCS versioning/lifecycle](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-versioning).

### P1 — State write and event publish are not atomic or idempotent

Evidence:

- Both ingest services save state, then publish separately: `cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:63-75`, `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:66-78`.
- A publish failure leaves durable state with no guaranteed event; retrying republishes.
- Events contain no event ID or schema version: `pkg/domain/events.go:11-17`, `pkg/domain/events.go:44-50`.
- Notification processing dispatches on every delivery with no deduplication: `cmd/notification-service/worker.go:64-116`.

Suggested issue: `feat(events): add transactional outbox and consumer idempotency`

Acceptance criteria:

- Define versioned envelopes with stable event ID, type, occurrence time, correlation/trace ID, and payload version.
- Atomically persist domain state and an outbox record.
- Reliably publish outbox records and track completion.
- Maintain consumer deduplication keyed by event ID and operation.
- Guarantee duplicate delivery cannot send duplicate notifications or regress state.
- Add crash-point and redelivery tests.

Dependencies/duplicates: #91 is adjacent but retry/DLQ alone does not fix the dual-write gap.

### P1 — Runtime configuration and secrets have no contract

Evidence:

- Cloud Run OpenTofu and manifests set no application environment or secret values.
- Current configuration is scattered defaults such as `PORT`, `OLLAMA_HOST`, and `OLLAMA_MODEL`: `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:13-16`, `pkg/ollama/client.go:45-56`, `cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:26-36`.
- Notification providers remain mocks with hard-coded recipients/tokens: `cmd/notification-service/worker.go:79-105`, `cmd/notification-service/dispatcher.go:44-125`.
- `.gitignore` allows an `.env.example`, but none exists: `.gitignore:8-14`.

Suggested issue: `feat(config): add validated config and Secret Manager integration`

Acceptance criteria:

- Central typed configuration per service with documented required/optional values.
- Production fails fast on missing bucket/topic/endpoint/provider config.
- Store provider credentials, session keys, and VAPID material in Secret Manager.
- Grant each service access only to its secrets and pin environment-secret versions.
- Use ADC for Google APIs; never set `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` in Cloud Run.
- Provide safe local examples and rotation/runbook tests.

Dependencies/duplicates: #65 supplies notification providers but does not cover secret lifecycle; stale #63 will introduce session secrets. [Cloud Run secrets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/secrets).

### P1 — Telemetry code is not an operating model

Evidence:

- #64 remains open.

- `/healthz` always returns OK without dependency checks: `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:798-802`.
- No monitoring, alert, SLO, uptime-check, or runbook resources exist.

Suggested issue: `feat(ops): provision SLOs, alerts, dashboards, and runbooks`

Acceptance criteria:

- Complete #64’s real OpenTelemetry/logging/readiness instrumentation first.
- Define user-facing availability/latency and report-to-notification freshness SLOs.
- Alert on Cloud Run 5xx/start failures, Pub/Sub backlog/oldest unacked/DLQ, Firestore errors, inference failures, and notification failure rate.
- Add synthetic checks and correlation across HTTP/event boundaries.

- Load-test and set per-service concurrency, CPU/memory, timeout, min/max instances.

- Label resources for allocation and publish an expected idle/normal/peak cost model.
- Add actual and forecast billing thresholds plus anomaly notifications.
- Add quota monitoring and a documented emergency cost-control response.
- Revisit thresholds after AI benchmark results.

Cloud Run currently recommends setting maximum instances as an initial cost safeguard. [Cloud Run maximum instances](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/max-instances), [budget alerts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets).

- Rewrite #91 around actual managed subscriptions and Cloud Run acknowledgement semantics.

Live GitHub inventory found 10 open issues, no GitHub environments, no Actions secrets or variables, and only the CI workflow. I could not inspect an actual GCP project, so this assesses repository readiness, not deployed state.

## Priority findings

### P0 — No durable shared runtime

Evidence:

- Every process creates an isolated in-memory backend: `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:18-20`, `cmd/foundpet-service/main.go:19-22`, `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:16-18`, `cmd/notification-service/main.go:13-15`, `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:31-34`.
- UI and service collection names disagree: `lost_pets` at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:297-300` versus `lostPets` at `cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:65-72`; likewise `found_pets` at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:440-443` versus `foundPets` at `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:68-75`.
- The matcher reads one hard-coded candidate, `lost-101`, at `cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:78-105`.
- The match API seeds fake production-looking matches when state is empty at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:480-556`.
- Only memory implementations exist in `pkg/store/store.go:25-109`, `pkg/pubsub/pubsub.go:22-62`, and `pkg/blob/blob.go:31-100`.

Suggested issue: `feat(runtime): implement one durable shared report-to-match path`

Acceptance criteria:

- Implement Firestore state and GCS blob adapters using ADC.
- Define canonical collections and production data models.
- Production startup must reject memory adapters.
- Remove automatic demo seeding and hard-coded candidate IDs from production mode.
- Run Firestore/Pub/Sub/storage emulators or equivalent shared local dependencies in Compose.
- Prove a report survives service restart and is visible to another process.
- Add an emulator-backed and deployed smoke test for one vertical cascade.

Dependencies/duplicates: closed #3, #23, #90, and #93 are stale or only implemented interfaces/UI wiring; #66 is infrastructure-only.

### P0 — Pub/Sub and the Cloud Run worker model do not work

Evidence:

- Each binary owns a separate `MemoryPubSub`, so publishers cannot reach subscribers across containers.
- OpenTofu creates topics only, with no subscriptions: `infra/opentofu/modules/pubsub/main.tf:1-11`.
- `pet-matcher` and `notification-service` never listen on `$PORT`: `cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:15-31`, `cmd/notification-service/main.go:13-26`.
- Both are nevertheless declared as Knative Cloud Run Services: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:1-18`, `deploy/cloudrun/notification-service.yaml:1-18`.

A Cloud Run Service ingress container must listen on its injected port. Google also recommends Pub/Sub push for Cloud Run services; pull-based workloads should deliberately use a worker pool instead. [Cloud Run container contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract), [Cloud Run autoscaling](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling), [subscription types](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-overview).

Suggested issue: `feat(pubsub): add authenticated Cloud Run push consumers`

Acceptance criteria:

- Add real Pub/Sub publishers and one subscription per consumer.
- Prefer authenticated push endpoints for matcher and notification handlers; otherwise document and provision worker pools.
- Grant the Pub/Sub push identity only `run.invoker` on its target.
- Return 2xx only after successful processing; temporary failures must produce redelivery.
- Provision ack/retry/retention/DLQ settings and DLQ subscriptions in OpenTofu.
- Verify authenticated delivery, redelivery, poison-message handling, and emulator/local behavior.

Dependencies/duplicates: #91 overlaps retry/DLQ but does not solve the missing transport or invalid Cloud Run execution model; its implementation proposal should be rewritten around subscription policy. Closed #22 promised subscriptions but created only topics.

### P0 — “Completed” GCS upload support is still a mock

Evidence:

- The upload handler constructs `MemoryBlobStore` per request: `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:772-795`.
- The generated URL contains literal `sig=mock-sig`: `pkg/blob/blob.go:75-99`.
- `foundpet-service` reserves but never uses the blob dependency: `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:14-27`.
- The storage bucket has no CORS or explicit public-access-prevention policy: `infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`.

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #62 rather than file a duplicate.

Additional acceptance criteria:

- Generate GCS V4 signed uploads with bounded object prefix, content type, size, and expiry.
- Verify object metadata before creating a found-pet record.
- Enforce bucket public-access prevention; signed URLs remain compatible with it.
- Restrict CORS to configured frontend origins and required methods/headers.
- Add orphan-upload cleanup and emulator/integration coverage.

Relevant guidance: [public access prevention and signed URLs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/public-access-prevention), [Cloud Storage CORS](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cross-origin).

### P0 — Authentication closure is stale; production exposure would expose mutations

Evidence:

- Routes are registered without authentication middleware at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71`.
- Anyone can confirm/reject matches at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:576-618`, send a purported “secure” contact message at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652`, or mark a pet reunited at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:661-699`.
- Lost-pet submissions accept reporter contact data at `cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267-300`.
- There is no user/session implementation in `go.mod:1-3` or the service startup path.

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #63.

Acceptance criteria:

- Integrate an OIDC provider or Identity Platform and validate sessions server-side.
- Enforce ownership/authorization on every state-changing or contact-data endpoint.
- Return redacted public DTOs.
- Add CSRF protection where cookie sessions are used.
- Audit authorization decisions and add negative integration tests.
- Make #94’s lifecycle endpoints depend on this work.

### P0 — Production AI inference is completely unprovisioned

Evidence:

- The client defaults to `http://localhost:11434`: `pkg/ollama/client.go:16`, `pkg/ollama/client.go:45-56`.
- The matcher manifest supplies no `OLLAMA_HOST`, model service, authentication, or GPU, and allocates only 2 CPU/2 GiB: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:9-18`.
- OpenTofu has no model-serving resource: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:16-39`.

Suggested issue: `feat(ai): provision private Gemma 4 inference for production`

Acceptance criteria:

- Record an architecture decision: private Cloud Run GPU Ollama versus managed Vertex AI.
- If retaining Ollama, provision an authenticated internal GPU Cloud Run service, set `OLLAMA_HOST`, model loading/startup probes, request timeout, concurrency, maximum instances, and quota.
- Do not expose Ollama publicly.
- Benchmark representative images for quality, p50/p95 latency, cold start, throughput, and cost.
- Add circuit breaking, bounded retries, and a user-visible deferred/retry state.
- Add model/version provenance to results.

Google now documents Gemma 4/Ollama on GPU Cloud Run, but it requires materially different resources and explicit cost/concurrency controls. [Gemma 4 with Ollama](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/tutorials/gpu-gemma-with-ollama), [Cloud Run GPU requirements](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu).

Evidence:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-187` contains validation only.
- All images use mutable `gcr.io/petspotr/*:latest`: `infra/opentofu/variables.tf:12-40` and every `deploy/cloudrun/*.yaml`.
- The deployment guide assumes an already-existing image and manually replaces a service: `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:82-105`.
- `Dockerfile:8` sends the entire repository into the build context, and there is no `.dockerignore`.
- GitHub currently has zero environments, Actions secrets, and variables.

Container Registry writes stopped in 2025; Artifact Registry is the supported target. [Artifact Registry transition](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/transition/transition-from-gcr).

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #13, preferably retitled `chore(cd): build and deploy immutable Cloud Run revisions`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Provision regional Artifact Registry repositories.
- Authenticate GitHub using Workload Identity Federation, never a service-account key.
- Build each image once per commit and deploy by digest.
- Generate SBOM/vulnerability results and fail on the agreed severity policy.
- Add protected staging/production GitHub environments and promotion rules.
- Choose one deployment authority—OpenTofu or manifests—and remove drift between them.
- Run post-deploy smoke checks, support traffic rollback, and record deployed SHA/digest.
- Add `.dockerignore` covering `.git`, local credentials, state, reports, and generated WIF credential files.

### P1 — Least-privilege identity and ingress are absent

Evidence:

- Cloud Run resources specify only name, location, and image: `infra/opentofu/modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-54`.
- No user-managed service accounts, IAM bindings, invoker policies, or ingress settings exist.
- Outputs call every service URL “Public”: `infra/opentofu/outputs.tf:1-24`.

Suggested action: expand/retitle open #66 to `feat(infra): enforce service identities and Cloud Run ingress`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Dedicated service account per service.
- Resource-scoped Firestore, Storage, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, and invoker roles.
- Only the intended browser entrypoint is unauthenticated.
- Matcher/notification endpoints accept only authenticated Pub/Sub delivery.
- Decide whether public traffic uses direct `run.app` or an external load balancer; if the latter, disable direct public ingress and add Armor/rate-limiting policy.
- Avoid the Compute Engine default service account.
- Add IAM policy tests and document the trust graph.

Google recommends user-managed identities with minimal roles and layered ingress plus IAM. [Cloud Run service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/service-identity), [Cloud Run ingress](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/ingress).

### P1 — Infrastructure cannot safely bootstrap or support environments

Evidence:

- No backend block or environment structure exists: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:1-39`.
- Required Google APIs are not enabled in code.
- The provider constraint is broad, `~> 5.0`: `infra/opentofu/main.tf:1-8`.
- `.terraform.lock.hcl` is ignored at `.gitignore:16-22`; the local ignored lock currently resolves old provider 5.45.2.
- Documentation directs developers to apply directly from a laptop: `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:82-89`.
- Infra tests check only file/resource-string existence: `infra/infra_test.go:10-39`.

Suggested issue: `chore(infra): add remote state and environment bootstrapping`

Acceptance criteria:

- Bootstrap a private, versioned, access-controlled GCS state bucket.
- Commit the dependency lock file and pin intentionally reviewed provider ranges.
- Separate dev/staging/prod projects or roots with explicit variables and labels.
- Enable required APIs declaratively.
- Add CI plan output, policy checks, approval-gated apply, and drift detection.
- Document ADC-based local planning; prohibit downloaded service-account keys.
- Add semantic IaC tests, not only string-existence checks.

Google recommends a Cloud Storage backend and automated plan/apply workflow. [Terraform security practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/best-practices/security), [Terraform operations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/best-practices/operations).

### P1 — Data protection, indexes, and disaster recovery are undefined

Evidence:

- Firestore is a bare regional database: `infra/opentofu/modules/firestore/main.tf:1-5`.
- No PITR, scheduled backup, deletion protection, TTL, or indexes exist.
- The bucket sets `force_destroy = true`: `infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`.
- Versioning is enabled without lifecycle limits, creating unbounded noncurrent-version cost.
- The region defaults to `us-central1` with no availability/RPO decision: `infra/opentofu/variables.tf:6-10`.

Suggested issue: `feat(data): define RPO, backups, indexes, and restore drills`

Acceptance criteria:

- Decide regional versus multi-region Firestore before first production creation.
- Set production deletion protection, PITR, and scheduled backups.
- Declare every required composite/geospatial/query index in code.
- Set `force_destroy=false` in production.
- Choose soft-delete/versioning/lifecycle policy and cap retained noncurrent versions.
- Define RPO/RTO and execute a documented Firestore and GCS restore drill.
- Monitor backup failures and storage growth.

Dependencies/duplicates: closed #93 covers API filtering, not Firestore indexing. No open issue covers recovery. [Firestore DR](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/disaster-recovery), [Firestore indexes as Terraform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/standard-indexing), [GCS versioning/lifecycle](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-versioning).

### P1 — State write and event publish are not atomic or idempotent

Evidence:

- Both ingest services save state, then publish separately: `cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:63-75`, `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:66-78`.
- A publish failure leaves durable state with no guaranteed event; retrying republishes.
- Events contain no event ID or schema version: `pkg/domain/events.go:11-17`, `pkg/domain/events.go:44-50`.
- Notification processing dispatches on every delivery with no deduplication: `cmd/notification-service/worker.go:64-116`.

Suggested issue: `feat(events): add transactional outbox and consumer idempotency`

Acceptance criteria:

- Define versioned envelopes with stable event ID, type, occurrence time, correlation/trace ID, and payload version.
- Atomically persist domain state and an outbox record.
- Reliably publish outbox records and track completion.
- Maintain consumer deduplication keyed by event ID and operation.
- Guarantee duplicate delivery cannot send duplicate notifications or regress state.
- Add crash-point and redelivery tests.

Dependencies/duplicates: #91 is adjacent but retry/DLQ alone does not fix the dual-write gap.

### P1 — Runtime configuration and secrets have no contract

Evidence:

- Cloud Run OpenTofu and manifests set no application environment or secret values.
- Current configuration is scattered defaults such as `PORT`, `OLLAMA_HOST`, and `OLLAMA_MODEL`: `cmd/lostpet-service/main.go:13-16`, `pkg/ollama/client.go:45-56`, `cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:26-36`.
- Notification providers remain mocks with hard-coded recipients/tokens: `cmd/notification-service/worker.go:79-105`, `cmd/notification-service/dispatcher.go:44-125`.
- `.gitignore` allows an `.env.example`, but none exists: `.gitignore:8-14`.

Suggested issue: `feat(config): add validated config and Secret Manager integration`

Acceptance criteria:

- Central typed configuration per service with documented required/optional values.
- Production fails fast on missing bucket/topic/endpoint/provider config.
- Store provider credentials, session keys, and VAPID material in Secret Manager.
- Grant each service access only to its secrets and pin environment-secret versions.

const common="Surfaced by the production-readiness audit on `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`.\n\n";

{
 title:"refactor(api): route web workflows through canonical services",
 labels:["agent-found"],
 body:common+`## Problem

The web frontend implements a second set of report APIs instead of using the report services:

- Browser code posts to the web process (\`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/lost-wizard.js:128-144\`, \`found-report.js:110-125\`).
- Web handlers save only to their private store and publish no events (\`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:206-308,352-451\`).
- The lost/found services use different collections and do publish events (\`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:63-75\`, \`cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:66-78\`).

A successful UI submission therefore bypasses the matcher cascade. Closed #90 connected handlers to an injected state interface but did not establish a shared or canonical application boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Record the intended boundary: web as a BFF calling private report services, or shared application commands invoked by both HTTP adapters.
- Keep one authoritative validation, persistence, event publication, error, and idempotency path per command.
- Route browser submissions through that path and remove duplicate business logic.
- Use explicit internal authentication for service-to-service calls in GCP.
- Preserve public API compatibility or version any intentional contract change.
- Return success only after the accepted durability/event-delivery guarantee is met.
- Add contract tests that run the same cases through direct service and browser-facing entrypoints.

Depends on #107 and #108; event reliability is tracked separately.`

{
 title:"feat(domain): define complete versioned report schemas",
 labels:["agent-found"],
 body:common+`## Problem

The forms collect meaningful product data, but the persisted events discard most of it.

\`LostPetFormRequest\` includes name, species, breed, colors, description, phone, and email, while \`LostPetEvent\` retains only ID, email, time, and a location string. The found form similarly loses finder contact, species, breed, colors, custody, and extracted traits (\`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:127-136,285-300,342-350,428-443\`; \`pkg/domain/events.go:11-17,44-50\`).

The current location is an unstructured string; unknown locations silently become Seattle center in \`pkg/domain/geo.go:45-74\`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define separate persisted aggregates, public DTOs, command requests, and versioned integration events.
- Persist stable IDs, owner/finder identity references, timestamps, status, species/breed/colors/markings, description, custody, verified image object references, and validated coordinates.
- Store private contact data separately from public listing data.
- Represent geocoding status explicitly; never substitute a default coordinate for unknown input.
- Define additive event evolution rules, schema version, stable event ID, and tolerant readers for in-flight messages.
- Validate lengths, enums, timestamps, coordinates, and normalized contact data at the boundary.
- Add migration/compatibility tests for every prior event shape already published by the app.

Complements #94 and is a prerequisite for real matching and notifications.`

The matcher reads only hard-coded \`lost-101\`, injects Golden Retriever traits, and publishes a transient result without persisting it (\`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:78-121\`). The web API then seeds two fake matches whenever the match store is empty (\`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:480-556\`). Unknown locations receive a Seattle fallback that can create a false proximity boost.

Closed #61 added scoring helpers but not real candidate retrieval/indexing. Closed #90 added a match-store read but the producer never writes that store.

## Acceptance criteria

- Query all eligible active lost reports within a bounded time/geographic candidate window.
- Use persisted, image-derived traits for both lost and found reports; remove hard-coded candidate IDs and traits.
- Reject or defer matching when required coordinates/images/traits are unavailable; never apply a default location.
- Rank candidates deterministically and persist match records with stable idempotency keys before emitting notifications.
- Store score components, distance, model/version, threshold version, timestamps, and explanation/provenance.
- Exclude closed/reunited/expired reports in coordination with #94.
- Remove automatic production match seeding; put demo fixtures behind an explicit development seed command.
- Add multi-candidate, no-candidate, duplicate-event, model-failure, and threshold-boundary tests.

Depends on #107, #108, the canonical schema issue, and #111.`

{
 title:"feat(events): add transactional outbox and idempotency",
 labels:["agent-found"],
 body:common+`## Problem

Both ingest services save state and then publish as separate operations (\`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:63-75\`, \`cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:66-78\`). A publish failure leaves durable state without a guaranteed event; a client retry can publish duplicates. Events have no stable event ID or schema version, and notification processing has no deduplication.

Open #91 adds retries/DLQs, but retries alone do not solve the dual-write gap or duplicate side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a versioned event envelope with stable event ID, type, occurrence time, correlation/trace ID, aggregate ID/version, and payload version.
- Atomically persist domain state and an outbox record.
- Reliably publish pending outbox records and record completion without losing crash recovery.
- Make every consumer idempotent using a durable deduplication key and operation/result record.
- Guarantee duplicate delivery cannot send duplicate notifications or regress report/match state.
- Define ordering/concurrency behavior for competing updates to the same aggregate.
- Add crash-point tests before/after persistence, publication, acknowledgement, and provider dispatch.
- Add redelivery tests coordinated with #91's retry and DLQ policies.

Depends on the durable store and managed Pub/Sub work in #107 and #108.`

 title:"feat(local): run the full cascade against shared emulators",
 labels:["agent-found","migration:gcp"],

\`docker compose up --build\` starts isolated service containers plus Ollama, but no shared state or event transport (\`docker-compose.yml:28-84\`). Closed #11 and #57 describe that outcome but do not currently deliver it.

- Add containerized Firestore and Pub/Sub emulators (and a safe GCS-compatible local adapter/fake) to Compose.

Official Firestore emulator: https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/emulator`
},
{
 title:"chore(infra): add remote state and environment bootstrapping",
 labels:["agent-found","migration:gcp"],
 body:common+`## Problem

OpenTofu has no backend or environment structure, does not enable required APIs, and uses a broad provider constraint (\`infra/opentofu/main.tf:1-39\`). The provider lock file is ignored by \`.gitignore\`. Documentation directs developers to apply directly from a laptop, and infra tests only assert that files/resources contain expected strings.

- Separate development, staging, and production projects/roots with explicit variables, labels, and guardrails.
- Enable required Google APIs declaratively.
- Add CI plan output, formatting/validation, policy checks, approval-gated apply, and scheduled drift detection.
- Use ADC and Workload Identity Federation; prohibit downloaded service-account keys.
- Prevent accidental cross-environment plans/applies and destructive production changes.
- Add semantic IaC tests for identities, ingress, subscriptions, deletion protection, and immutable images.
- Document state recovery and lock/concurrency procedures.

Google Terraform security practices: https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/terraform/best-practices/security`
},
{
 title:"feat(data): define backups indexes and restore drills",
 labels:["agent-found","migration:gcp"],
 body:common+`## Problem

Firestore is a bare database with no deletion protection, PITR, backup schedule, TTL policy, or declared indexes (\`infra/opentofu/modules/firestore/main.tf:1-5\`). The image bucket sets \`force_destroy=true\` and enables versioning without lifecycle bounds (\`infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9\`). Regional/multi-region, RPO, and RTO choices are undocumented.

Closed #93 adds in-memory filtering, not Firestore indexes or recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide and document regional versus multi-region Firestore before production creation.
- Set production deletion protection, point-in-time recovery, and scheduled backups.
- Declare required composite/geospatial/query indexes in code.
- Set production image storage to \`force_destroy=false\`.
- Choose soft-delete/versioning/lifecycle retention and cap noncurrent versions and orphan uploads.
- Define retention for reports, matches, events, push subscriptions, and audit records.
- Define RPO/RTO and execute documented Firestore and GCS restore drills.
- Monitor backup failures, restore readiness, and storage growth.
- Verify user deletion/export workflows do not destroy evidence or backups contrary to policy.

Firestore backup guidance: https://cloud.google.com/firestore/docs/backups`
},
{
 title:"feat(config): validate runtime config and integrate secrets",
 labels:["agent-found","migration:gcp"],
 body:common+`## Problem

Runtime configuration is scattered across implicit defaults for \`PORT\`, \`OLLAMA_HOST\`, and \`OLLAMA_MODEL\`. Cloud Run resources set no application environment or secret values. Notification workers use mock providers and hard-coded recipients/tokens. \`.gitignore\` permits a safe \`.env.example\`, but none exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define centralized typed configuration per service with documented required, optional, default, and sensitive values.
- Validate configuration before serving/consuming and fail production startup on missing bucket, project, collection, topic/subscription, endpoint, identity, or provider values.
- Store session keys, notification credentials, VAPID material, and other secrets in Secret Manager.
- Grant each runtime identity access only to its secrets and pin environment-secret versions deliberately.
- Use ADC for Google APIs; do not mount or set service-account JSON credentials in Cloud Run.
- Provide a non-secret \`.env.example\` and Compose defaults that work with emulators.
- Document rotation, rollback, local overrides, and redaction rules.
- Add tests for invalid modes, missing values, secret resolution, and log redaction.

## Related

Provider integration remains tracked in #65; service IAM remains part of #66.`
},
{
 title:"feat(ops): provision SLOs alerts dashboards and runbooks",
 labels:["agent-found","migration:gcp"],
 body:common+`## Problem

Open #64 tracks instrumentation and probes, but the repository has no monitoring resources, service-level objectives, alert policies, uptime checks, notification channels, or runbooks. Existing JSON logger and pseudo-tracer are unused by service mains; no code records web request metrics, and \`/healthz\` always returns OK.

This extends rather than duplicates #64.`

 labels:["agent-found","migration:gcp"],

Cloud Run OpenTofu defines no concurrency, timeout, min/max instances, or resource policy (\`infra/opentofu/modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-54\`). Worker manifests disable CPU throttling, and the proposed AI path can add GPU cost. No budget, forecast, anomaly, or quota alerts exist.

Cloud Run maximum instances: https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/max-instances

Cloud Billing budgets: https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets`

Follow-up to closed #55 and #60; depends on #107, #110, #114, and the filtering issue.`

Pagination slices values collected from a Go map (\`pkg/store/store.go:91-109\`), whose iteration order is undefined, so page contents can duplicate or disappear between requests. ## Bottom line

PetSpotR is currently a polished in-process demo, not yet a functioning multi-process local app or deployable GCP application. The most serious gap is that every process owns a separate in-memory broker/store, so the documented Compose event cascade cannot occur. Many closed roadmap issues were closed after interfaces or UI shells landed, even though their end-to-end acceptance criteria remain unmet.

PetSpotR is currently a polished in-process demo, not yet a functioning multi-process local app or deployable GCP application. 2. `docs(architecture): define canonical API, service, and event ownership`

Evidence: the web service duplicates report APIs (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:206-451`), while lost/found services expose separate `/lostPet` and `/foundPet` contracts (`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:37-82`, `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:40-85`). Store names also diverge: `lostPets`/`foundPets` versus `lost_pets`/`found_pets`.

Acceptance:

- Decide whether web is a BFF calling report services or the sole ingestion service.
- Assign ownership of reports, matches, uploads, contact messages, and lifecycle transitions.
- Document local and GCP request/event topology.
- Define failure ownership, retry boundaries, and service-to-service authentication.
- Remove duplicate handler paths in follow-up slices.

Dependencies: none.  
Overlap: closed #90 describes the symptom but did not resolve the boundary.

3. `refactor(frontend): submit reports through canonical services`

Evidence: browser code posts to the web service (`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/lost-wizard.js:128-144`, `cmd/web-frontend/static/js/found-report.js:110-125`). Those handlers only save to the web process’s private store and never publish (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:285-300`, `:428-443`). The actual report services persist and publish separately (`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:65-74`, `cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:68-77`).

Acceptance:

- Route both browser journeys through the canonical report API.
- Preserve and validate all submitted fields.
- Propagate dependency failures honestly to the UI.
- Emit the canonical event exactly once.
- Show success only after the durable ingestion boundary succeeds.

Dependencies: issues 1–2.  
Overlap: reopen closed #51, #52, and #90.

4. `feat(domain): define versioned pet report, public DTO, and event schemas`

Evidence: the lost form accepts name, species, breed, color, description, location, email, and phone (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:127-136`) but stores only ID, email, timestamp, and location (`:285-300`; `pkg/domain/events.go:11-17`). Found-pet traits, finder email, and custody status are similarly discarded (`server.go:342-350`, `:428-443`; `pkg/domain/events.go:44-50`). Public GET returns the stored `LostPetEvent`, including `reporterEmail` (`server.go:206-258`).

Acceptance:

- Define canonical persisted entities separately from public redacted DTOs and events.
- Preserve species, breed, colors, description, images, coordinates, custody, and status.
- Separate private reporter/finder contact records.
- Add event ID, schema version, correlation ID, and occurrence time.
- Define backward-compatible decoding and a migration strategy.
- Add OpenAPI/JSON Schema contract validation and consumer tests.

Dependencies: architecture ADR.  
Overlap: reopen closed #61, #63, and #92; coordinate with open #94.

5. `feat(images): implement verified local and GCS upload pipeline`

Evidence: lost-photo selection is preview-only (`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/lost-wizard.js:103-116`) and absent from the submitted payload (`:128-137`). Found images are browser data URLs embedded in JSON (`found-report.js:54-65`, `:110-125`) but the API body is capped at 1 MiB (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:413-424`). The “presigned” endpoint returns a synthetic `mock-sig` URL (`pkg/blob/blob.go:75-99`; `server.go:777-795`), and the found service’s blob store is unused (`cmd/foundpet-service/service.go:14-19`).

Acceptance:

- Provide working local and GCS direct-upload implementations.
- Validate MIME type, byte size, image dimensions, object ownership, and completed upload metadata.
- Persist image references in reports and serve/display them.
- Reject missing or incomplete uploads.
- Clean abandoned/orphaned objects.
- Exercise the entire browser upload journey.

Dependencies: issues 1 and 4.  
Overlap: reopen closed #51 and #62.

6. `feat(matcher): evaluate active candidates and persist idempotent matches`

Evidence: matcher reads only hardcoded `lost-101`, injects Golden Retriever traits, and exits when that record is absent (`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:78-105`). It publishes but never persists a match (`:108-121`). Web GET seeds two fake match records whenever the store is empty (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:492-556`). Unknown or blank locations silently map to Seattle center (`pkg/domain/geo.go:45-74`), creating false spatial similarity (`pkg/scoring/scorer.go:79-100`).

Acceptance:

- Query all eligible active candidates using deterministic pagination.
- Use persisted report traits/images rather than hardcoded traits.
- Treat missing/invalid coordinates as unknown, with no proximity boost.
- Persist a deterministic match ID, score breakdown, model version, and timestamps before publishing.
- Make processing idempotent under duplicate delivery.
- Exclude resolved/expired reports.
- Remove production seed-on-read behavior.

Dependencies: issues 1, 4, 5 and open #94; coordinate with open #91.  
Overlap: closed #61 and #90 were incomplete.

7. `fix(matcher): send validated image bytes to Ollama inference`

Evidence: the matcher passes `foundEvt.ImageURL` directly in Ollama’s `images` array (`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:60-69`). Ollama’s REST API requires base64-encoded image data, not a URL, per the [official vision documentation](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/vision). Existing integration tests use fake strings and a mock server that never validates the payload (`pkg/scoring/integration_test.go:15-84`).

Acceptance:

- Fetch image content only from trusted application storage.
- Enforce type, size, decoding, and pixel limits.
- Send raw base64 in the Ollama REST request.
- Classify corrupt image, transient inference, and invalid model-output failures.
- Add a payload-validating integration test and an opt-in real-model smoke test.

Dependencies: issue 5.  
Overlap: no current issue covers this defect.

8. `feat(infra): deploy event workers with a supported Cloud Run delivery topology`

Evidence: pet-matcher and notification are declared as Cloud Run Services (`infra/opentofu/modules/cloudrun/main.tf:34-54`; `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:1-18`; `notification-service.yaml:1-18`) but neither process listens on `PORT` (`cmd/pet-matcher/main.go:15-31`; `cmd/notification-service/main.go:13-26`). No Pub/Sub subscriptions or Eventarc triggers exist; the Pub/Sub module only creates topics (`infra/opentofu/modules/pubsub/main.tf:1-22`). Cloud Run services must listen on the injected port under Google’s [container runtime contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract).

Acceptance:

- Select Pub/Sub push/Eventarc HTTP handlers or a deliberately configured worker-pool topology.
- Provision subscriptions/triggers, DLQs, identities, IAM, and authenticated invocation.
- Implement the corresponding delivery/ack contract.
- Configure matcher model hosting or `OLLAMA_HOST`; the current standalone matcher otherwise defaults to localhost (`pkg/ollama/client.go:45-55`).
- Add deployed smoke tests.

Dependencies: issues 1–2; open #91.  
Overlap: rewrite open #66 rather than filing a parallel infrastructure issue.

### P1 — Credible development and product experience

9. `chore(dev): add reproducible fast and full-AI local profiles`

Evidence: local setup is only `docker compose up --build` (`README.md:40-60`; `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:28-67`). There is no Makefile/task runner, `.env.example`, `.dockerignore`, tool-version selector, bootstrap script, or smoke command. Docker builds with Go 1.22 (`Dockerfile:2`) while CI verifies 1.26.5 (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:65-77`). Only Ollama has a health check (`docker-compose.yml:4-26`). The default model is currently a roughly 7.2 GB download according to the [Ollama model registry](https://ollama.com/library/gemma4).

Acceptance:

- Pin/select Go, Node, OpenTofu, and other required tool versions.
- Add a one-command prerequisite check, bootstrap, start, smoke, logs, and teardown workflow.
- Provide a fast deterministic AI-stub profile and an explicit full-Ollama profile.
- Add health checks and dependency waiting for every service.
- Add configurable ports and documented environment defaults.
- Support source-mounted/hot-reload development where practical.
- Print actionable URLs and diagnostics on startup failure.

Dependencies: issues 1–2.  
Overlap: reopen #11; #88 only solved model pulling.

10. `feat(dev): add emulator-backed seed, reset, and schema migration tooling`

Evidence: Compose contains no Firestore, Pub/Sub, or object-storage emulator (`docker-compose.yml:3-87`); only the Ollama volume persists. No seed, migration, index, or reset files exist. The Firestore module creates only a database (`infra/opentofu/modules/firestore/main.tf:1-10`).

Acceptance:

- Start Firestore and Pub/Sub emulators plus a GCS-compatible local store.
- Create topics/subscriptions/buckets and deterministic representative seed records.
- Add explicit safe reset and reseed commands.
- Version stored documents.
- Add idempotent, resumable, dry-run-capable migration tooling.
- Track required Firestore indexes and test migrations against the emulator.
- Preserve data across normal Compose restarts.

Dependencies: runtime adapters and domain schema.  
Overlap: closed #3 and #11.

11. `fix(api): make filtering and pagination deterministic and contract-accurate`

Evidence: `status` is parsed but never applied (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:168-170`, `:206-259`, `:352-405`). Species is discarded on write, and the filter silently lets records without species through (`:220-229`, `:366-375`). Pagination slices values from a Go map with undefined iteration order (`pkg/store/store.go:91-109`; `server.go:242-253`). Tests only assert that the desired result is present, not that excluded data is absent (`cmd/web-frontend/server_test.go:428-453`; `tests/playwright/e2e/web-frontend-api.spec.ts:179-185`).

Acceptance:

- Persist and enforce every supported filter.
- Reject malformed coordinates, radii, limits, and incomplete geo queries.
- Use a stable indexed sort and cursor pagination.
- Ensure page boundaries cannot duplicate or omit records.
- Remove the unknown-location Seattle fallback.
- Add negative filter and multi-page tests.

Dependencies: issues 1 and 4; open #94.  
Overlap: reopen closed #61, #92, and #93.

12. `fix(api): enforce authorized atomic match and reunion transitions`

Evidence: match actions return 200 even when the match does not exist (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:601-617`). “Secure contact” validates two strings, stores/sends nothing, and always reports success (`:626-651`). Reunion resolution updates only a match if found, never the lost/found report, but always returns `REUNITED` (`:661-699`). All routes are unauthenticated.

Acceptance:

- Require authentication and ownership/authorized-role checks.
- Return 404 for missing resources and 409 for invalid transitions.
- Apply a defined state machine transactionally across match and report records.
- Persist contact messages and feedback or deliver them through the notification boundary.
- Emit versioned, idempotent state-change events.
- Never expose reporter contact details in public list APIs.

Dependencies: domain schema and shared store.  
Overlap: extend open #94 and reopen closed #63/#54 rather than duplicate.

13. `feat(frontend): restore a real public pet directory and search journey`

Evidence: every navigation shell links to `/pets` (`cmd/web-frontend/templates/layout.html:22-27`, `report-lost.html:22-27`, `report-found.html:22-27`, `matches.html:22-27`), but no `/pets` route exists (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-72`), so it falls through to 404 (`:74-77`). The “interactive map” is static text (`report-lost.html:104-118`).

Acceptance:

- Implement `/pets` with real active report data.
- Provide grid and accessible map/list alternatives.
- Support text, species, breed/color, date, status, and validated radius filters.
- Synchronize filter state with the URL.
- Provide detail, empty, loading, and error states.
- Exercise mobile/tablet/desktop journeys.

Dependencies: issues 1, 4, 5, and 11.  
Overlap: reopen closed #55 and #60.

14. `fix(frontend): make reporting and match journeys keyboard and screen-reader accessible`

Evidence: CSS defines hover states but no focus-visible or reduced-motion treatment (`cmd/web-frontend/static/css/styles.css:172-226`), and hides navigation below 768px without a replacement (`:296-310`). Upload surfaces are non-focusable `<div>` elements with hidden file inputs (`report-lost.html:88-101`, `report-found.html:43-76`) and bind only mouse click/drop (`lost-wizard.js:75-101`, `found-report.js:21-46`). Modals lack dialog semantics, focus management, and keyboard dismissal (`matches.html:62-138`). Playwright config defines no device projects (`tests/playwright/playwright.config.ts:3-17`).

Acceptance:

- Restore accessible mobile navigation.
- Make upload controls native or keyboard-operable with announced errors/progress.
- Add focus-visible, reduced-motion, and accessible step-status behavior.
- Give dialogs correct roles, labels, focus trap/restore, and Escape behavior.
- Replace blocking alerts with inline/live-region validation.
- Run automated accessibility checks and browser journeys at representative viewports.

Overlap: closed #50–#60 claimed this coverage but did not deliver it.

15. `feat(notifications): add preferences, subscription lifecycle, and delivery status`

Evidence: match delivery uses hardcoded owner email, phone, and push token (`cmd/notification-service/worker.go:79-106`); community subscribers are hardcoded sample Seattle residents (`broadcast.go:35-55`); all senders are mocks (`dispatcher.go:44-126`). Browser push uses a mock VAPID key (`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/push-notifier.js:47-56`), subscription storage is private memory (`server.go:724-755`), and `/push/test` only returns JSON (`:757-769`).

Acceptance:

- Extend open #65 with real configurable providers and local capture providers.
- Add subscribe, update-preferences, and unsubscribe flows.
- Store subscriptions under authenticated ownership.
- Support radius/channel preferences and consent.
- Persist delivery attempts/status and expire invalid endpoints.
- Connect notification links to a specific authorized match.
- Add local Mailpit/push test UX.

Dependencies: shared runtime and authentication.  
Overlap: extend open #65; coordinate with #91.

16. `feat(data): implement retention, deletion, backup, and orphan cleanup`

Evidence: no report deletion/expiry or lifecycle implementation exists; open #94 only proposes statuses. GCS is provisioned with `force_destroy = true` and versioning but no lifecycle policy (`infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`). Contact, feedback, delivery records, and uploaded-object cleanup are absent.

Acceptance:

- Define retention periods for active, resolved, expired, contact, push, and model-feedback data.
- Cascade authorized deletion/redaction across reports, matches, contact data, subscriptions, and images.
- Expire abandoned uploads and stale reports.
- Configure Firestore recovery/export and GCS lifecycle/version-retention policy.
- Add audited administrative cleanup and restoration procedures.

Dependencies: canonical schema, authentication, and status lifecycle.

### P1 — Verification and delivery

17. `test(e2e): exercise the real browser-to-worker-to-notification cascade`

Evidence: Go “E2E” tests reimplement service handlers instead of using production code (`e2e/e2e_test.go:21-85`) and register custom in-process subscribers (`:121-198`). The web cascade test constructs action/reunion requests but never sends them through a handler or asserts responses (`e2e/web_frontend_cascade_test.go:160-174`). CI starts only lost, found, and web services (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:101-102`); browser coverage only verifies four page bodies are visible (`tests/playwright/e2e/web-frontend-api.spec.ts:137-143`). Readiness uses `curl` without `--fail`, so any HTTP response counts as ready (`ci.yml:107-127`).

Acceptance:

- Run production binaries against shared local emulators.
- Drive upload and both report forms through a browser.
- Await persisted match generation and captured notification delivery.
- Confirm authorized contact/reunion and state propagation.
- Exercise duplicate delivery and transient dependency failure.
- Test mobile/tablet/desktop with screenshots/traces/logs.
- Use real dependency-aware health checks.
- Make the suite required once stable.

Dependencies: runtime, images, matcher, notification, and lifecycle work.  
Overlap: reopen closed #56–#60 and #67.

18. `test(ai): establish real-model compatibility and match-quality evaluation`

Evidence: the only opt-in live test still uses `gemma2:2b`, sends no image, and merely asserts non-nil traits (`pkg/scoring/integration_test.go:87-111`). The current production default is `gemma4:e2b` (`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:25-36`). The home page’s 98.4% accuracy claim has no supporting evaluation (`templates/layout.html:58-70`).

Acceptance:

- Add a small licensed, privacy-safe image corpus with match/non-match labels.
- Verify the configured model accepts real image payloads and meets JSON-schema parse targets.
- Record false-positive/false-negative, threshold, latency, and resource metrics.
- Version evaluation results with model/prompt changes.
- Run a fast compatibility smoke test regularly and a fuller opt-in/nightly evaluation.
- Remove unsupported accuracy claims until measured.

19. `chore(release): build immutable images and promote verified GCP releases`

Evidence: the only workflow is CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-187`). Closed #13 promised `deploy-gcp.yml`, but none exists. OpenTofu and manifests default to hardcoded `gcr.io/petspotr/...:latest` (`infra/opentofu/variables.tf:12-39`; `deploy/cloudrun/*.yaml`). Docker uses a different Go toolchain than CI (`Dockerfile:2`; `ci.yml:65-77`).

Acceptance:

- Build all service images with the verified toolchain.
- Publish to Artifact Registry using commit-SHA tags and immutable digests.
- Authenticate with Workload Identity Federation.
- Promote through staging and approval-gated production.
- Run post-deploy smoke/cascade checks and retain rollback targets.
- Expose build/version metadata.
- Produce release notes plus image provenance/SBOM.

Dependencies: deployable runtime, #64, rewritten #66, and real E2E.

## Existing issue disposition

- Keep and expand #64: health/readiness must cover all five workloads and actual dependency readiness, not just synthetic 200s.
- Extend #65 with preference, consent, unsubscribe, and delivery-state acceptance criteria.
- Keep #91, but add transactional outbox/idempotency as a prerequisite; retries/DLQ alone cannot repair save-then-publish partial failure (`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:65-74`).
- Keep #94 and make it the canonical status-state-machine issue.
- Rewrite #66: its literal frontend-manifest acceptance criteria are already present (`infra/opentofu/main.tf:31-39`, `modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-10`, `deploy/cloudrun/web-frontend.yaml:1-17`), while the real IAM/config/event-delivery gaps are absent.
- #48, #49, and #104–#106 are valid workflow/docs-test debt but do not move product readiness.
- Reopen or supersede closed #3, #9, #11, #13, #51–#63, #67, #90, #92, and #93. Their issue bodies contain substantial acceptance criteria that current code does not satisfy.

## Documentation and product-trust cleanup

A final lower-priority issue should reconcile documentation and demo behavior:

`docs(roadmap): replace stale migration claims with an evidence-based readiness roadmap`

The migration plan still references Gemma 2 and Dapr (`docs/MIGRATION_PLAN.md:1-22`) despite the code defaulting to Gemma 4 and containing no Dapr adapters. It marks every item unchecked while most referenced issues are closed (`:45-165`). Development docs describe notification channels and GCP deployment as working (`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:10-24`, `:71-105`) when only mocks and resource shells exist. The public UI also fabricates product metrics and unconditional operational status (`templates/layout.html:58-80`) and success modals claim indexing/matching that never occurs (`report-lost.html:143-151`, `report-found.html:145-153`).

const r = await tools.mcp__codex_apps__github_create_issue({
  repository_full_name:"scottdensmore/PetSpotR",
  title:"fix(frontend): prevent stored DOM injection in match rendering",
  labels:["agent-found"],
  body:`## Problem

The match dashboard renders persisted match fields by interpolating them into an HTML string and assigning the result to \`innerHTML\`. Once real reports and persisted matcher output replace the current seed data, attacker-controlled pet names, breeds, locations, image URLs, or IDs can become stored DOM injection.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on \`main\` at \`09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb\`.

## Evidence

- \`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41\` assigns concatenated match-card markup to \`container.innerHTML\`.
- \`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:45-139\` interpolates \`matchId\`, pet name, breed, location, image URL, status, and score fields into HTML, attributes, and inline styles without contextual encoding.
- \`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:555-572\` returns persisted match documents directly to the browser.
- \`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-71\` registers the application without a response-security-header middleware; there is no Content Security Policy to reduce impact.

## Acceptance criteria

- Construct match cards with DOM APIs and \`textContent\`, or apply proven contextual encoding for text and attribute values.
- Validate image URLs against the application-owned storage policy before assigning them to \`src\`.
- Treat match IDs and numeric score/style values as typed, validated data rather than markup.
- Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and baseline response headers without relying on CSP as the primary injection fix.
- Remove inline script/style dependencies needed to enforce the chosen CSP.
- Add browser tests containing HTML, quote, and script-like payloads in every rendered persisted field and assert they remain inert.
- Cover both server-seeded/test fixtures and the future canonical persisted-match path.

## Scope

This issue is distinct from #110, which covers authentication, ownership, and contact privacy. It addresses browser-side output handling and defense in depth.`

  title:"feat(security): add abuse controls to public endpoints",
  labels:["agent-found"],
  body:`## Problem

The public web process exposes report creation, feature extraction/inference, upload signing, push subscription/test, contact, and lifecycle mutation endpoints with no rate limiting, quota enforcement, bot friction, or request-cost controls. Per-request body limits are useful but do not prevent repeated requests, storage exhaustion, notification abuse, or expensive model invocation.

Surfaced during the repository readiness audit on \`main\` at \`09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb\`.

## Evidence

- \`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:60-69\` registers every API directly on the public mux.
- \`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:267\`, \`:320\`, \`:413\`, \`:582\`, \`:632\`, \`:667\`, and \`:730\` cap individual bodies but provide no caller- or route-level request budget.
- \`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:308-340\` performs feature extraction on submitted image data, an expensive path once real inference is connected.
- \`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:626-652\` and \`:724-769\` expose contact and push operations without delivery-abuse controls.
- No rate-limiter, challenge, moderation queue, Cloud Armor policy, quota middleware, or abuse telemetry exists in \`cmd/\`, \`pkg/\`, or \`infra/\`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a threat and cost model for anonymous report, upload, inference, contact, and notification operations.
- Apply per-IP and, after authentication, per-account quotas with stricter route-specific limits for expensive or externally billable work.
- Add bounded concurrency and queue/backpressure controls around inference and notification delivery.
- Require single-use, short-lived upload intents and enforce storage/object quotas.
- Add bot/spam defenses appropriate to the public reporting journey without blocking accessibility.
- Record privacy-safe abuse metrics and alert on rejection rate, unusual spend, inference saturation, and notification spikes.
- Define trusted-proxy/IP handling and test header spoofing before using client IP as an identity signal.
- Add deterministic tests for burst, sustained, concurrent, and distributed-limit behavior.
- Provision edge controls in code if the production ingress uses an external Application Load Balancer/Cloud Armor.

## Scope

This complements #110 (identity/authorization), #109 (secure upload lifecycle), #111 (AI hosting), #121 (SLOs/alerts), and #122 (cost guardrails). Those issues do not define request-level abuse prevention.`

## Bottom line

PetSpotR is currently a polished in-process demo, not yet a functioning multi-process local app or deployable GCP application. The most serious gap is that every process owns a separate in-memory broker/store, so the documented Compose event cascade cannot occur. Many closed roadmap issues were closed after interfaces or UI shells landed, even though their end-to-end acceptance criteria remain unmet.
