11. `fix(api): make filtering and pagination deterministic and contract-accurate`

Evidence: `status` is parsed but never applied (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:168-170`, `:206-259`, `:352-405`). Species is discarded on write, and the filter silently lets records without species through (`:220-229`, `:366-375`). Pagination slices values from a Go map with undefined iteration order (`pkg/store/store.go:91-109`; `server.go:242-253`). Tests only assert that the desired result is present, not that excluded data is absent (`cmd/web-frontend/server_test.go:428-453`; `tests/playwright/e2e/web-frontend-api.spec.ts:179-185`).

Acceptance:

- Persist and enforce every supported filter.
- Reject malformed coordinates, radii, limits, and incomplete geo queries.
- Use a stable indexed sort and cursor pagination.
- Ensure page boundaries cannot duplicate or omit records.
- Remove the unknown-location Seattle fallback.
- Add negative filter and multi-page tests.

Dependencies: issues 1 and 4; open #94.  
Overlap: reopen closed #61, #92, and #93.

12. `fix(api): enforce authorized atomic match and reunion transitions`

Evidence: match actions return 200 even when the match does not exist (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:601-617`). “Secure contact” validates two strings, stores/sends nothing, and always reports success (`:626-651`). Reunion resolution updates only a match if found, never the lost/found report, but always returns `REUNITED` (`:661-699`). All routes are unauthenticated.

Acceptance:

- Require authentication and ownership/authorized-role checks.
- Return 404 for missing resources and 409 for invalid transitions.
- Apply a defined state machine transactionally across match and report records.
- Persist contact messages and feedback or deliver them through the notification boundary.
- Emit versioned, idempotent state-change events.
- Never expose reporter contact details in public list APIs.

Dependencies: domain schema and shared store.  
Overlap: extend open #94 and reopen closed #63/#54 rather than duplicate.

13. `feat(frontend): restore a real public pet directory and search journey`

Evidence: every navigation shell links to `/pets` (`cmd/web-frontend/templates/layout.html:22-27`, `report-lost.html:22-27`, `report-found.html:22-27`, `matches.html:22-27`), but no `/pets` route exists (`cmd/web-frontend/server.go:47-72`), so it falls through to 404 (`:74-77`). The “interactive map” is static text (`report-lost.html:104-118`).

Acceptance:

- Implement `/pets` with real active report data.
- Provide grid and accessible map/list alternatives.
- Support text, species, breed/color, date, status, and validated radius filters.
- Synchronize filter state with the URL.
- Provide detail, empty, loading, and error states.
- Exercise mobile/tablet/desktop journeys.

Dependencies: issues 1, 4, 5, and 11.  
Overlap: reopen closed #55 and #60.

14. `fix(frontend): make reporting and match journeys keyboard and screen-reader accessible`

Evidence: CSS defines hover states but no focus-visible or reduced-motion treatment (`cmd/web-frontend/static/css/styles.css:172-226`), and hides navigation below 768px without a replacement (`:296-310`). Upload surfaces are non-focusable `<div>` elements with hidden file inputs (`report-lost.html:88-101`, `report-found.html:43-76`) and bind only mouse click/drop (`lost-wizard.js:75-101`, `found-report.js:21-46`). Modals lack dialog semantics, focus management, and keyboard dismissal (`matches.html:62-138`). Playwright config defines no device projects (`tests/playwright/playwright.config.ts:3-17`).

Acceptance:

- Restore accessible mobile navigation.
- Make upload controls native or keyboard-operable with announced errors/progress.
- Add focus-visible, reduced-motion, and accessible step-status behavior.
- Give dialogs correct roles, labels, focus trap/restore, and Escape behavior.
- Replace blocking alerts with inline/live-region validation.
- Run automated accessibility checks and browser journeys at representative viewports.

Overlap: closed #50–#60 claimed this coverage but did not deliver it.

15. `feat(notifications): add preferences, subscription lifecycle, and delivery status`

Evidence: match delivery uses hardcoded owner email, phone, and push token (`cmd/notification-service/worker.go:79-106`); community subscribers are hardcoded sample Seattle residents (`broadcast.go:35-55`); all senders are mocks (`dispatcher.go:44-126`). Browser push uses a mock VAPID key (`cmd/web-frontend/static/js/push-notifier.js:47-56`), subscription storage is private memory (`server.go:724-755`), and `/push/test` only returns JSON (`:757-769`).

Acceptance:

- Extend open #65 with real configurable providers and local capture providers.
- Add subscribe, update-preferences, and unsubscribe flows.
- Store subscriptions under authenticated ownership.
- Support radius/channel preferences and consent.
- Persist delivery attempts/status and expire invalid endpoints.
- Connect notification links to a specific authorized match.
- Add local Mailpit/push test UX.

Dependencies: shared runtime and authentication.  
Overlap: extend open #65; coordinate with #91.

16. `feat(data): implement retention, deletion, backup, and orphan cleanup`

Evidence: no report deletion/expiry or lifecycle implementation exists; open #94 only proposes statuses. GCS is provisioned with `force_destroy = true` and versioning but no lifecycle policy (`infra/opentofu/modules/storage/main.tf:1-9`). Contact, feedback, delivery records, and uploaded-object cleanup are absent.

Acceptance:

- Define retention periods for active, resolved, expired, contact, push, and model-feedback data.
- Cascade authorized deletion/redaction across reports, matches, contact data, subscriptions, and images.
- Expire abandoned uploads and stale reports.
- Configure Firestore recovery/export and GCS lifecycle/version-retention policy.
- Add audited administrative cleanup and restoration procedures.

Dependencies: canonical schema, authentication, and status lifecycle.

### P1 — Verification and delivery

17. `test(e2e): exercise the real browser-to-worker-to-notification cascade`

Evidence: Go “E2E” tests reimplement service handlers instead of using production code (`e2e/e2e_test.go:21-85`) and register custom in-process subscribers (`:121-198`). The web cascade test constructs action/reunion requests but never sends them through a handler or asserts responses (`e2e/web_frontend_cascade_test.go:160-174`). CI starts only lost, found, and web services (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:101-102`); browser coverage only verifies four page bodies are visible (`tests/playwright/e2e/web-frontend-api.spec.ts:137-143`). Readiness uses `curl` without `--fail`, so any HTTP response counts as ready (`ci.yml:107-127`).

Acceptance:

- Run production binaries against shared local emulators.
- Drive upload and both report forms through a browser.
- Await persisted match generation and captured notification delivery.
- Confirm authorized contact/reunion and state propagation.
- Exercise duplicate delivery and transient dependency failure.
- Test mobile/tablet/desktop with screenshots/traces/logs.
- Use real dependency-aware health checks.
- Make the suite required once stable.

Dependencies: runtime, images, matcher, notification, and lifecycle work.  
Overlap: reopen closed #56–#60 and #67.

18. `test(ai): establish real-model compatibility and match-quality evaluation`

Evidence: the only opt-in live test still uses `gemma2:2b`, sends no image, and merely asserts non-nil traits (`pkg/scoring/integration_test.go:87-111`). The current production default is `gemma4:e2b` (`cmd/pet-matcher/worker.go:25-36`). The home page’s 98.4% accuracy claim has no supporting evaluation (`templates/layout.html:58-70`).

Acceptance:

- Add a small licensed, privacy-safe image corpus with match/non-match labels.
- Verify the configured model accepts real image payloads and meets JSON-schema parse targets.
- Record false-positive/false-negative, threshold, latency, and resource metrics.
- Version evaluation results with model/prompt changes.
- Run a fast compatibility smoke test regularly and a fuller opt-in/nightly evaluation.
- Remove unsupported accuracy claims until measured.

19. `chore(release): build immutable images and promote verified GCP releases`

Evidence: the only workflow is CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-187`). Closed #13 promised `deploy-gcp.yml`, but none exists. OpenTofu and manifests default to hardcoded `gcr.io/petspotr/...:latest` (`infra/opentofu/variables.tf:12-39`; `deploy/cloudrun/*.yaml`). Docker uses a different Go toolchain than CI (`Dockerfile:2`; `ci.yml:65-77`).

Acceptance:

- Build all service images with the verified toolchain.
- Publish to Artifact Registry using commit-SHA tags and immutable digests.
- Authenticate with Workload Identity Federation.
- Promote through staging and approval-gated production.
- Run post-deploy smoke/cascade checks and retain rollback targets.
- Expose build/version metadata.
- Produce release notes plus image provenance/SBOM.

Dependencies: deployable runtime, #64, rewritten #66, and real E2E.

## Existing issue disposition

- Keep and expand #64: health/readiness must cover all five workloads and actual dependency readiness, not just synthetic 200s.
- Extend #65 with preference, consent, unsubscribe, and delivery-state acceptance criteria.
- Keep #91, but add transactional outbox/idempotency as a prerequisite; retries/DLQ alone cannot repair save-then-publish partial failure (`cmd/lostpet-service/service.go:65-74`).
- Keep #94 and make it the canonical status-state-machine issue.
- Rewrite #66: its literal frontend-manifest acceptance criteria are already present (`infra/opentofu/main.tf:31-39`, `modules/cloudrun/main.tf:1-10`, `deploy/cloudrun/web-frontend.yaml:1-17`), while the real IAM/config/event-delivery gaps are absent.
- #48, #49, and #104–#106 are valid workflow/docs-test debt but do not move product readiness.
- Reopen or supersede closed #3, #9, #11, #13, #51–#63, #67, #90, #92, and #93. Their issue bodies contain substantial acceptance criteria that current code does not satisfy.

## Documentation and product-trust cleanup

A final lower-priority issue should reconcile documentation and demo behavior:

`docs(roadmap): replace stale migration claims with an evidence-based readiness roadmap`

The migration plan still references Gemma 2 and Dapr (`docs/MIGRATION_PLAN.md:1-22`) despite the code defaulting to Gemma 4 and containing no Dapr adapters. It marks every item unchecked while most referenced issues are closed (`:45-165`). Development docs describe notification channels and GCP deployment as working (`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:10-24`, `:71-105`) when only mocks and resource shells exist. The public UI also fabricates product metrics and unconditional operational status (`templates/layout.html:58-80`) and success modals claim indexing/matching that never occurs (`report-lost.html:143-151`, `report-found.html:145-153`).

Acceptance should require clearly separated demo and production modes, honest empty states, live dependency status, and roadmap status verified against code plus GitHub issue state."}},{"agent_name":"/root/security_product","agent_status":"interrupted"}]}

content.text:
## Outcome

PetSpotR is currently a polished in-memory demo, not yet a functioning multi-process local application or production-ready GCP system.

I audited `main` at `09f96e4596192bb0d5a15a7780628854c9afaddb`, reconciled open and closed issues, reviewed local development, GCP infrastructure, product behavior, security boundaries, CI/CD, and filed 23 net-new issues: [#107–#129](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3Aagent-found).

### The fundamental blocker

Every executable creates its own `MemoryStore` and `MemoryPubSub`. Consequently:

- Reports submitted through the browser never reach the report services.
- Events cannot cross Compose containers.
- State disappears on restart.
- The matcher and notification worker cannot receive another process’s events.
- Local and Cloud Run deployments cannot produce the documented cascade.

The web frontend also maintains duplicate APIs and different collection names, while the matcher uses a hardcoded lost-pet ID, hardcoded traits, and fake matches seeded on reads.

### GCP blockers

- Matcher and notification are declared as Cloud Run Services but never listen on `$PORT`, violating the [Cloud Run container contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract).
- Pub/Sub infrastructure creates topics but no subscriptions, authenticated push identities, retries, or DLQs. Cloud Run services should generally use authenticated [Pub/Sub push delivery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/authenticate-push-subscriptions), unless worker pools are chosen deliberately.
- GCS uploads are mocks containing `sig=mock-sig`.
- Firestore has no production adapters, indexes, PITR/backups, deletion protection, or restore process.
- No service identities, least-privilege IAM, ingress policy, Secret Manager integration, remote OpenTofu state, environment separation, or declarative API enablement exists.
- Deployment uses mutable `gcr.io/...:latest` images with no CD workflow. New delivery should use Artifact Registry and immutable digests; Google documents the [Container Registry transition](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/transition/transition-from-gcr).
- Production inference is undefined. Matcher defaults to local Ollama, while its Cloud Run configuration has no model endpoint or GPU. Cloud Run GPU inference needs materially different resource, concurrency, quota, and cost decisions under the [GPU requirements](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu).

### Product and security blockers

- Report schemas discard most entered pet, image, custody, and contact fields.
- Lost-pet listing can return reporter email.
- Match/contact/reunion mutations are unauthenticated and report success for nonexistent or unperformed work.
- Matcher passes an image URL to Ollama where validated image bytes/base64 are required.
- `/pets` is linked throughout the UI but returns 404.
- Filtering and pagination are nondeterministic or silently ineffective.
- Match rendering interpolates persisted fields into `innerHTML`, creating a stored DOM-injection path once real user data reaches matches.
- Public upload, inference, notification, and contact endpoints have no abuse controls.
- Accessibility gaps include missing mobile navigation, mouse-only uploads, inaccessible dialogs, and absent focus/reduced-motion handling.
- Public claims such as 98.4% accuracy, sub-three-second matching, and operational success are unsupported by real evaluation or infrastructure.

## Filed backlog

The recommended implementation order is:

1. Runtime and contracts: [#107](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/107), [#113](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/113), [#114](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/114).
2. Identity and safe ingestion: [#109](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/109), [#110](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/110), [#128](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/128), [#129](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/129).
3. Event delivery and local emulators: [#108](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/108), [#116](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/116), [#117](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/117).
4. Real matching and inference: [#123](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/123), [#111](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/111), [#115](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/115).
5. Infrastructure and delivery: [#118](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/118), [#120](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/120), [#112](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/112).
6. Reliability and operations: [#119](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/119), [#121](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/121), [#122](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/122).
7. Product completion: [#124](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/124), [#125](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/125), [#126](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/126), [#127](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/127).

Existing #64, #65, #66, #91, and #94 remain relevant, but need the new runtime work as prerequisites. Numerous closed issues—including #3, #11, #13, #22, #23, #51–#63, #90, #92, and #93—were only partially completed; the new issues capture their remaining work as smaller verifiable slices.

## Verification and limitations

- `go test ./...` passed using Go 1.26.5.
- Docker Compose configuration validates, with only the obsolete top-level `version` warning.
- The worktree remains clean and synchronized with `origin/main`.
- No source files or infrastructure state were changed.
- OpenTofu validation was not run because `tofu` is not installed locally.
- No actual GCP project was inspected, so this assesses repository readiness rather than current deployed resources.
- The independent deep-security scanner failed to return after bounded retries. The two security issues filed were manually validated, but this should not be represented as a completed formal deep-security scan.

The best first implementation slice is [#107](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/107): introduce the durable runtime adapter selection and prove one report can cross process boundaries and survive restart.

+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `memory` | None | Process-local memory | Unit tests and demo-only development |

## Priority findings

Evidence:

Acceptance criteria:

- Implement Firestore state and GCS blob adapters using ADC.
- Define canonical collections and production data models.
- Production startup must reject memory adapters.

Evidence:

- Both are nevertheless declared as Knative Cloud Run Services: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:1-18`, `deploy/cloudrun/notification-service.yaml:1-18`.

A Cloud Run Service ingress container must listen on its injected port. Google also recommends Pub/Sub push for Cloud Run services; pull-based workloads should deliberately use a worker pool instead. [Cloud Run container contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract), [Cloud Run autoscaling](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling), [subscription types](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-overview).

Suggested issue: `feat(pubsub): add authenticated Cloud Run push consumers`

- Prefer authenticated push endpoints for matcher and notification handlers; otherwise document and provision worker pools.
- Grant the Pub/Sub push identity only `run.invoker` on its target.
- Return 2xx only after successful processing; temporary failures must produce redelivery.

- Verify authenticated delivery, redelivery, poison-message handling, and emulator/local behavior.

Dependencies/duplicates: #91 overlaps retry/DLQ but does not solve the missing transport or invalid Cloud Run execution model; its implementation proposal should be rewritten around subscription policy. Closed #22 promised subscriptions but created only topics.

Suggested action: reopen stale closed issue #62 rather than file a duplicate.

Additional acceptance criteria:

- Generate GCS V4 signed uploads with bounded object prefix, content type, size, and expiry.
- Verify object metadata before creating a found-pet record.
- Enforce bucket public-access prevention; signed URLs remain compatible with it.
- Restrict CORS to configured frontend origins and required methods/headers.
- Add orphan-upload cleanup and emulator/integration coverage.

Relevant guidance: [public access prevention and signed URLs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/public-access-prevention), [Cloud Storage CORS](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cross-origin).

Evidence:

### P0 — Pub/Sub and the Cloud Run worker model do not work

Evidence:

- Both are nevertheless declared as Knative Cloud Run Services: `deploy/cloudrun/pet-matcher.yaml:1-18`, `deploy/cloudrun/notification-service.yaml:1-18`.

A Cloud Run Service ingress container must listen on its injected port. Google also recommends Pub/Sub push for Cloud Run services; pull-based workloads should deliberately use a worker pool instead. Suggested issue: `feat(pubsub): add authenticated Cloud Run push consumers`

Acceptance criteria:

- Add real Pub/Sub publishers and one subscription per consumer.
- Prefer authenticated push endpoints for matcher and notification handlers; otherwise document and provision worker pools.
- Grant the Pub/Sub push identity only `run.invoker` on its target.
- Return 2xx only after successful processing; temporary failures must produce redelivery.
- Provision ack/retry/retention/DLQ settings and DLQ subscriptions in OpenTofu.
- Verify authenticated delivery, redelivery, poison-message handling, and emulator/local behavior.
